'''Karl Rebane''' (11 April 1926 – 4 November 2007)<ref name="A.Rebane 2008">{{cite web| url=http://www.physics.montana.edu/faculty/rebane/Rebane/Karl_Rebane/2008.htm| title=Karl Rebane| date=4 November 2008| publisher=Aleksander Rebane| access-date=31 December 2012| archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130916041036/http://www.physics.montana.edu/faculty/rebane/Rebane/Karl_Rebane/2008.htm| archive-date=16 September 2013| url-status=dead}}</ref> was an [[Estonia]]n [[physicist]].

== Biography ==
He studied at the [[Tallinn University of Technology|Tallinn Technical University]] from 1947 to 1949, and graduated from the [[Saint Petersburg State University|Leningrad University]] in 1952. He graduated from Leningrad University in 1955 with a doctorate in solid state theory. He also obtained a [[Doctor of Sciences]] in Theoretical Physics in 1964 from the Belarusian AS. He became a faculty member at [[University of Tartu|Tartu University]] in 1955. He was Professor and Chair of the Experimental Physics Department between 1958 and 1960, and was Professor and Chair of the Joint Department of Laser Optics at the Institute of Physics between 1974 and 1993.<ref>{{cite web |doi=10.1063/PT.4.2165 |doi-access=free | url=http://www.physicstoday.org/obituaries/1.2528498| archive-url=https://archive.today/20130415174706/http://www.physicstoday.org/obituaries/1.2528498| url-status=dead| archive-date=15 April 2013| title=Obituary of Karl Rebane |website=Physics Today | date=25 February 2008 |first1=Joseph |last1=Birman |first2=Anshel |last2=Gorokhovsky |first3=Alexei |last3=Maradudin |first4=Alexander |last4=Kaplyanskii}}</ref> He was president of the [[Estonian Academy of Sciences]] from 1973 to 1990.<ref>{{cite web| url=http://www.fi.ut.ee/183055| title=History of the UT Institute of Physics| language=Estonian| date=4 January 2011| publisher=University of Tartu| access-date=30 December 2012| archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120226163233/http://www.fi.ut.ee/183055| archive-date=26 February 2012| url-status=dead}}</ref>

==Early life==
Karl Rebane was born in [[Pärnu]], Estonia.<ref name="A.Rebane 2008"/> His father, Karl Rebane Sr., was a bookkeeper.<ref name="KarlRebane90">{{cite web |last1=Sammelselg |first1=Tiina |title=Karl Rebane 90 |url=https://www.fi.ut.ee/et/instituudist/karl-rebane-90 |website=Tartu Ülikooli Füüsika Instituut |date=6 December 2016 |access-date=25 May 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210224234023/https://www.fi.ut.ee/et/instituudist/karl-rebane-90 |archive-date=24 Feb 2021 |language=Estonian}}</ref> He was the second oldest out of five children.<ref name="KarlRebane90"/> His brothers were {{ill|Jaan Rebane|et|Jaan Rebane}}, Toomas Rebane ([[:et:Toomas Rebane|:et]]) and {{ill|Jüri Rebane|et|Jüri Rebane}}.<ref name="KarlRebane90"/> The war reached Estonia in 1941 and his family evacuated to a small village in the oblast of [[Chelyabinsk Oblast|Chelyabinsk]] where he worked at the local [[kolkhoz]] and attended a school for displaced Estonian children in [[Verkhneuralsk]].<ref name="A.Rebane 2008"/> In the spring of 1944, he was called into military service and joined [[8th Estonian Rifle Corps|''Eesti Laskurkorpus'']], an Estonian division of the [[Red Army]], where he was a crew member of a 45 mm antitank gun.<ref name="A.Rebane 2008"/><ref name="Estonian AS 2021"/> He was wounded in battle on November 23, 1944, on the [[Sõrve peninsula]], Estonia.<ref name="A.Rebane 2008"/><ref name="Estonian AS 2021"/>

==Awards and honours==
''For research and scientific activity:''
*1965 – {{ill|Estonian SSR National Prize|et|Nõukogude Eesti preemia}}<ref name="Estonian AS 2021">{{cite web |title=Karl Rebane |url=https://www.akadeemia.ee/wp-content/uploads/2020/02/rebane.pdf |website=Eesti Teaduste Akadeemia |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200927220125/https://www.akadeemia.ee/wp-content/uploads/2020/02/rebane.pdf |access-date=22 May 2021 |archive-date=2020-09-27 |language=Estonian}}</ref>
*1976 – [[Order of the Red Banner of Labour]]
*1981 – {{ill|P. N. Lebedev Gold Medal|ru|Золотая медаль имени П. Н. Лебедева}} from the [[Academy of Sciences of the Soviet Union]] for achievements in the field of Physics<ref name="Estonian AS 2021" />
*1986 – {{ill|Medal of the Estonian Academy of Sciences|et|Eesti Teaduste Akadeemia medal}}<ref name="Estonian AS 2021" />
*1986 – [[Hero of Socialist Labour]], [[Order of Lenin]]<ref name="Estonian AS 2021" />
*1993 – [[Humboldt Research Award]] (Germany)<ref name="Estonian AS 2021" />
*1996 – [[Estonian National Research Awards|Estonian National Research Award]] (as part of a collective) for research work in exact sciences, chemistry, and biology<ref name="Estonian AS 2021" />
*2000 – [[Order of Friendship]]<ref name="Estonian AS 2021" />
*2001 – [[Estonian National Research Awards|Estonian National Research Award]] for outstanding lifetime achievements in research and development<ref name="Estonian AS 2021" />
*2002 – [[Royal Norwegian Order of Merit]]<ref name="Estonian AS 2021" />
*2003 – Cariplo Research Fellowship (Italy)<ref name="Estonian AS 2021" />
*2006 – [[Order of the White Star]], 3rd class<ref name="Estonian AS 2021" />

==Family==
He was married to [[Ljubov Rebane]], and had two children, Inna and [[Aleksander Rebane]]. He also had three brothers, Jaan, Toomas, and Jüri Rebane.{{cn|date=April 2026}}
